                    ### Question
                    An investigator studying the immunologic profile of various cells notices that the blood of a test subject agglutinates upon addition of a serum containing antibodies against P blood group antigens. Infection with which of the following pathogens would most likely be prevented by these antibodies?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Parvovirus B19
opb. Babesia microti
opc. Plasmodium vivax
opd. Epstein Barr virus
ope. Influenza virus

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Antibodies against P blood group antigens would most likely prevent infection by Parvovirus B19, as it utilizes the P antigen for cell entry. Other pathogens listed (Babesia microti, Plasmodium vivax, Epstein Barr virus, Influenza virus) do not use the P antigen, hence antibodies against these antigens would not prevent infections caused by these pathogens.
